structural_memory.memory: Lubricating-oil service spans owner/manager, master, engineering crew, shore technical/procurement support, lubricating-oil supplier or testing actors, filter/purifier equipment or service actors and relevant port/yard support. Product supply, onboard service state, assurance and equipment support should remain distinct roles rather than one vendor directory.

Product or grade identity confidence and oil-condition/quality confidence are distinct states. Knowing the intended lubricant does not prove its measured condition, fitness, compatibility, contamination state or machinery outcome; exact grades, viscosities and specifications remain deferred.

Storage inventory/capacity confidence is separate from active supply or circulation readiness. Lubricating oil can be onboard while usable replenishment margin, service-tank availability or intended consumer supply remains constrained or uncertain; exact quantities and tank arrangements are deferred.

Supply/circulation-pump readiness and distribution/path availability are separate states. A pump can be available while one branch or consumer path is restricted, or a path can be intact while circulation capacity or redundancy confidence is degraded; exact pressures, flows, piping and valve lineups are deferred.

Filtering or purification equipment readiness is distinct from achieved oil-condition confidence. Equipment being online does not itself establish acceptable cleanliness, water content, contamination state, viscosity or machinery protection; exact filter/purifier parameters and results remain deferred.

Sampling, testing or trend-confidence should remain separate from physical oil condition and circulation availability. Missing, delayed, conflicting or scoped assurance can leave condition uncertain without proving degraded oil, while a machinery symptom does not by itself prove an oil-condition cause.

Lubricating-oil cooling support is a dependency state distinct from circulation and oil condition. Adequate circulation does not prove acceptable thermal condition, and a temperature concern does not establish an oil-cooler or machinery-cooling root cause; exact temperatures and exchanger details are deferred.

Consumption, leakage or replenishment-margin confidence is distinct from exact consumption rate and from waste-oil generation. Declining usable inventory can constrain service margin without proving leakage, abnormal consumption, contamination, transfer error or machinery defect; exact rates and quantities remain deferred.

Lubricating-oil degradation has a defensive lifecycle: observation, uncertain product/inventory/pump/filter/purifier/path/consumer scope, affected service dimension, restriction or unavailability, bounded isolation, restoration indication and post-restoration verification. No transfer, purification, sampling or machinery troubleshooting procedure is retained.

Restriction or isolation should preserve affected oil grade/product, storage/service scope, pump/filter/purifier path or machinery consumer group. Partial lubricating-oil service may remain available while one branch or consumer is constrained; exact tank, piping, valve and changeover arrangements remain deferred.

Lubricating-oil service depends on electrical power, circulation equipment, cooling, controls/monitoring and sometimes treatment equipment, but dependency observations are not root-cause proof. A support-service loss can degrade oil service, while an oil-service constraint does not establish an electrical, cooling, digital or mechanical cause.

Lubricating-oil-service degradation can propagate into machinery availability, load restriction or condition concern, but downstream vibration, temperature, wear or availability effects do not themselves prove a lubricant product, contamination, inventory, pump, filter, purifier or cooling root cause.

Restoration can have multiple timestamps: product/inventory confidence returns, circulation and distribution return, filtering/purification service returns, oil-condition confidence becomes acceptable, replenishment margin is restored and affected machinery is re-verified. A restarted pump or purifier alone does not prove full lubricating-oil-service recovery.

P075 machinery oily-waste service and P080 lubricating-oil service are independent chains. Waste-oil/sludge holding or reception does not prove lubricating-oil inventory, circulation or condition, and lubricating-oil availability does not establish waste-handling capacity.

P077 bunker fuel and P080 lubricating oil share petroleum-product supply, storage and assurance vocabulary but have different service purposes, consumer scopes, condition states and downstream effects. Fuel availability or quality confidence cannot proxy lubricating-oil service and vice versa.

P079 machinery-cooling service can support lubricating-oil thermal condition, but acceptable cooling does not prove lubrication circulation or oil condition, and an oil-temperature concern does not establish a cooling-water root cause.

P067 equipment lifecycle should keep pumps, filters, purifiers, coolers, sensors and test equipment separate from delivered lubricating-oil service. Sound equipment can coexist with product, inventory, assurance or distribution constraints, and acceptable service does not prove every component condition.
Equipment readiness, maintenance, shore support and lifecycle mechanics overlap the generic marine-equipment lifecycle recovered in P067.

Scoped degradation, dependency, restriction/isolation, redundancy and verified-restoration mechanics overlap the defensive service-state patterns recovered in P068-P079; P080 applies them specifically to lubricating-oil service.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact lubricating-oil grades/specifications/viscosities, tank arrangements/capacities/quantities, pressures, temperatures, flow rates, filter/purifier settings, sample methods/results, piping, valves and instrumentation are intentionally not retained.

Exact lubricant receiving/transfer, circulation alignment, filter or purifier operation/changeover, sampling, replenishment, cooling, isolation, flushing, troubleshooting, maintenance or emergency procedures are outside this blind pass.

Named lubricant suppliers, laboratories, filter/purifier vendors, service firms, vessel installations, oil-condition disputes, failures, incidents, deficiencies and current-readiness facts require claim-scoped Evidence.
Private/regional lubricant supply/testing and filtration/purification service lineages plus historical non-English terminology remain deferred for source archaeology.

epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive lubricating-oil service orientation/source-discovery output. It is not lubricant selection, transfer, filtration/purification, sampling, machinery, maintenance, safety or vessel-operating advice and does not establish any exact grade, viscosity, quantity, arrangement, pressure, temperature, flow rate, filter/purifier parameter, sample result, piping/valve lineup, instrumentation, procedure, provider, incident, deficiency or current-readiness fact.
stop_reason: The lubricating-oil service chain is recalled at useful structural resolution: product/grade confidence, inventory/capacity confidence, supply/circulation and distribution readiness, filtering/purification readiness, condition/assurance confidence, cooling dependency, consumption/replenishment margin, restriction/isolation, dependencies, downstream effects and verified restoration are separable states. Further detail would become vessel-, grade-, tank-, pump-, filter-, purifier-, sample-, parameter-, piping-, procedure-, provider- or incident-specific and is deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
